failure_summary.description: Agents reran searches for covered scopes, reapplied criteria already in cached results, or searched instead of retrieving results after the user added no preference.
Agents mis-mapped state abbreviations, omitted a named neighborhood, or normalized an attraction type instead of preserving the requested value.
New attraction searches were not assigned to a variable and saved to cache.

patch.reasoning: The skill already gives explicit location-mapping and assign-and-save rules, so repeating them would not address a documentation gap. These edits clarify the remaining ambiguity in cache follow-ups: filter calls should contain only constraints not already embodied in their input, and a response declining additional preferences should use the already-covered cached results rather than start another search.

edits.target: Apply the matching `filter_*` tool with newly supplied filterable criteria, retaining constraints already embodied in the cached result.
edits.content: When filtering a compatible cached result, pass only newly supplied constraints and still-active supported constraints not already embodied in that selected result. Do not re-pass criteria already represented in it.

edits.target: - If an affirmative accepts only an offer to present recommendations from an already covered scope, retrieve the relevant cached result for use; do not repeat its search or an already-applied filter, or save a duplicate filtered result. Apply a filter only if the reply adds a new constraint.
edits.content: - If the user accepts an offer to present recommendations from an already covered scope, or answers a preference-clarification question without adding a constraint (for example, “not really”), retrieve the relevant cached result for use. Do not repeat its search, reapply an embodied filter, or save a duplicate result. Filter and save only when the reply adds a new constraint.
